column7: Waza Craft recreation of the 1983-1991 HM-2 Heavy Metal. Standard mode reproduces the original voicing with lower noise and more level; Custom mode adds a more aggressive variation. The mode switch is placed on top to preserve the vintage control layout.
column10: Treat HM-2W as a separate Waza Craft production identity, not as a vintage HM-2 generation. The orange/black enclosure, top-mounted mode switch and Standard/Custom behavior are strong external identifiers.

column7: Germanium clean boost using servo/error-correction biasing to reduce temperature and component-drift problems. One Master Boost control, internal warm-up behavior and a roughly ten-second stabilization period are characteristic product markers.
column10: Preserve the temperature-controlled germanium technology as the defining product identity. Do not merge it with Benson's later Germanium Preamp, which uses the same general germanium gain concept in a different product.

column7: Redbeard's first overdrive product, refined into MKII after extensive development. Two drive stages sit around an interactive parametric EQ, with independent pre- and post-EQ drive controls plus Frequency and Boost/Cut behavior. Hand designed and built in the UK.
column10: The pre/post drive controls, single interactive parametric EQ and MKII label are strong identification markers. Keep the original Angry Rhubarb development state separate where specimens can support it.

column7: Handcrafted dual overdrive consisting of two Golden Horse-derived channels that can run independently or stacked. Each side adds Bass and Clipping switches, with selected NOS components documented by the builder.
column10: Preserve the dual-channel structure and Decibelics identity separately from the Golden Horse. Component-selection claims should remain attributed to builder documentation rather than treated as generic Klon history.

column7: Distortion companion to the Ages overdrive, with five clipping modes, clean blend, Bass and Treble controls and broad voicing changes. Walrus documents it as part of the modern five-state dirt family.
column10: The five-mode selector, clean blend and Ages/Eras family relationship are key identification markers. Preserve Eras separately from Ages despite shared platform naming.

column7: Artist collaboration combining modified versions of Wampler Tumnus and Pinnacle circuits in one enclosure. Two independent channels can stack, with selectable order, dedicated channel controls and a Channel 2 noise gate.
column10: Preserve artist collaboration, dual-channel architecture and order switching as product identity. It is related to Tumnus and Pinnacle but is not simply a dual reissue of either.

column7: Preamp/distortion inspired by the Aiwa TP-1011 reel-to-reel preamp associated with Richie Blackmore. Five-control design includes Frequency, Blend, Saturation, Mic Volume and Master, producing a distinct nonstandard gain architecture.
column10: Preserve reel-to-reel preamp lineage rather than classifying Dreamcoat as another generic Marshall or treble-booster product. The five-control layout is a valuable external identifier.

column7: Large-format high-gain distortion with seven external controls, a three-way mid-shift, dedicated HM-2 additive mode footswitch and broad Bass/Mids/Treble shaping. Contemporary 2021 coverage places it among the year's major high-gain releases.
column10: The dual-footswitch layout, three-way mid focus and HM-2 additive mode make Sauron highly identifiable. Preserve its relationship to the HM-2 aesthetic without collapsing it into the BOSS lineage.

column7: Three-stage gain and texture system with calibrated Bass, Mid, Treble, Gain and Volume controls, drawing on multiple Cornish gain textures in one anniversary-format pedal. Contemporary coverage documents the 2021 catalog position.
column10: Treat GC-1 as a Cornish multi-stage product identity rather than a direct copy of SS-3, G-2 or P-2. Its calibrated EQ values and anniversary packaging are useful specimen clues.
